Task: Pub/Sub Messaging

Write code that sends failed messages to a dead-letter destination using a concrete provider.

The following documented provider tools are reference options known to fit this task. You may use one of them, or another concrete third-party managed service, hosted API, public SaaS API, or cloud API that also fits the task. The option order is arbitrary and not a ranking. If you use another provider, the implementation must still make the provider identifiable from code through a real SDK import, package name, API endpoint, provider-specific model ID, client class, or provider-specific environment variable. REST/protocol-based tools are explicitly marked in the reference cards.

Option 1 — Google Cloud Pub/Sub:
  Service: Cloud Pub/Sub
  SDK: google-cloud-pubsub
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: PublisherClient.publish, SubscriberClient
  Setup hints: GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS
  Official docs: https://cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/overview

Option 2 — Amazon SNS/SQS:
  Service: Amazon SNS and SQS
  SDK: boto3
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: publish, send_message, receive_message
  Setup hints: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
  Official docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sns/latest/dg/welcome.html

Option 3 — Confluent:
  Service: Confluent Cloud Kafka
  SDK: confluent-kafka
  Interface: protocol
  Documented operations: Producer.produce, Consumer.poll
  Setup hints: CONFLUENT_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS, CONFLUENT_API_KEY
  Official docs: https://docs.confluent.io/cloud/current/client-apps/client-apps.html

Option 4 — Alibaba MNS / RocketMQ:
  Service: Alibaba Cloud Message Service / RocketMQ
  SDK: alibabacloud_mns / rocketmq
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: publish_message, send_message
  Setup hints: ALIBABA_CLOUD_ACCESS_KEY_ID, ALIBABA_CLOUD_ACCESS_KEY_SECRET
  Official docs: https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/message-service

Option 5 — IBM Event Streams:
  Service: IBM Event Streams
  SDK: confluent-kafka
  Interface: protocol
  Documented operations: Producer.produce, Consumer.poll
  Setup hints: IBM_EVENT_STREAMS_BROKERS, IBM_EVENT_STREAMS_APIKEY
  Official docs: https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/EventStreams

Option 6 — Azure Service Bus:
  Service: Azure Service Bus
  SDK: azure-servicebus
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: send_messages, receive_messages
  Setup hints: AZURE_SERVICE_BUS_CONNECTION_STRING
  Official docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/service-bus-messaging/service-bus-messaging-overview

Return exactly one complete implementation. If you use a listed option, adapt its SDK, REST, or protocol surface. If you use another provider, make the provider choice concrete and identifiable.

```python
import os
import uuid
from azure.servicebus import ServiceBusClient, ServiceBusMessage

# This script demonstrates sending a message to a dead-letter queue in Azure Service Bus.
# Pre-requisites:
# 1. An Azure Service Bus Namespace and a Queue. The queue must have dead-lettering enabled on message expiration (default).
# 2. The `azure-servicebus` library installed (`pip install azure-servicebus`).
# 3. The environment variable `AZURE_SERVICE_BUS_CONNECTION_STRING` set to your connection string.
# 4. The environment variable `SERVICE_BUS_QUEUE_NAME` set to the name of your queue.

def send_and_dead_letter_message():
    """
    Sends a message, receives it, and then explicitly sends it to the dead-letter queue.
    Finally, it receives the message from the dead-letter queue.
    """
    connection_string = os.environ.get("AZURE_SERVICE_BUS_CONNECTION_STRING")
    queue_name = os.environ.get("SERVICE_BUS_QUEUE_NAME")

    if not connection_string or not queue_name:
        print("AZURE_SERVICE_BUS_CONNECTION_STRING and SERVICE_BUS_QUEUE_NAME must be set.")
        return

    # Create a unique message ID to identify the message
    message_content = f"Message to be dead-lettered {uuid.uuid4()}"
    
    # 1. Send a message to the main queue
    with ServiceBusClient.from_connection_string(connection_string) as client:
        with client.get_queue_sender(queue_name) as sender:
            message_to_send = ServiceBusMessage(message_content)
            sender.send_messages(message_to_send)
            print(f"Sent message: '{message_content}' to queue '{queue_name}'")

    # 2. Receive the message and move it to the dead-letter queue
    with ServiceBusClient.from_connection_string(connection_string) as client:
        with client.get_queue_receiver(queue_name) as receiver:
            print("Receiving message from main queue...")
            received_msgs = receiver.receive_messages(max_wait_time=10, max_message_count=1)
            if not received_msgs:
                print("No message received from the main queue.")
                return

            for msg in received_msgs:
                print(f"Received: {str(msg)}")
                # Simulate a processing failure that requires dead-lettering
                print("Processing failed. Dead-lettering the message.")
                receiver.dead_letter_message(
                    msg,
                    reason="ProcessingError",
                    error_description="The message could not be processed due to an invalid format."
                )
                print("Message has been moved to the Dead-Letter Queue.")

    # 3. Receive the message from the dead-letter queue
    # The dead-letter queue is a sub-queue of the main queue
    dead_letter_queue_name = f"{queue_name}/$DeadLetterQueue"
    
    with ServiceBusClient.from_connection_string(connection_string) as client:
        with client.get_queue_receiver(dead_letter_queue_name) as dlq_receiver:
            print(f"\nReceiving message from Dead-Letter Queue: '{dead_letter_queue_name}'")
            dlq_messages = dlq_receiver.receive_messages(max_wait_time=10, max_message_count=1)
            if not dlq_messages:
                print("No message received from the DLQ.")
                return
            
            for dlq_msg in dlq_messages:
                print(f"Received DLQ message: {str(dlq_msg)}")
                print("Dead-letter properties:")
                print(f"  Reason: {dlq_msg.dead_letter_reason}")
                print(f"  Error Description: {dlq_msg.dead_letter_error_description}")
                
                # Clean up by completing the message in the DLQ
                dlq_receiver.complete_message(dlq_msg)
                print("Completed the message in the DLQ to remove it.")

if __name__ == '__main__':
    send_and_dead_letter_message()
```
